blockers.quote: Restart near minute nine, the room of yes: you are surrounded by agreement and alone in it; nobody corrects you; the Challenger launch, analysed later through groupthink, is drawn as one paper diagram that draws itself, and your project goes ahead in the same breath.
blockers.why: Check #14 fails: the back half is denser than the front. This section compresses the stage failure, Milgram, the room of yes, Challenger, the project's launch, the friend's departure, the dilemma, the wordless peak and the honest answer into roughly the final quarter.
blockers.fix: Move the unanimous project commitment and group-scale image to the 40–50% office sequence, cut Challenger, and leave the 65–90% section as: stage failure therefore friend objects, friend leaves, paper dilemma, wordless answer.

suggestions.quote: Therefore the one person you have not asked, your friend, says it is wrong, and that is why he comes to return the last of the money and leave.
suggestions.fix: Replace with: "Therefore your friend—the one person still willing to tell you no without being asked—says the project is wrong, returns the last of the money, and leaves." He was already asked for the loan.

suggestions.quote: one sentence, "stay?", would keep him in the room, and he is the only no left that could stop the project; but his staying would be your yes, not his.
suggestions.fix: Before "stay?", establish the concrete action his voluntary dissent could take to stop the project, such as withdrawing the approval at the next meeting.
